Title: BN-Pas pact signals beginning of Malay-Muslim unity, says Akmal
Article:
MELAKA: The Melaka election will mark the beginning of a renewed push for Malay-Muslim political unity following a finalised electoral understanding between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pas.
Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh welcomed the agreement, saying it would help realise the Tekad Ummah initiative aimed at uniting Umno and Pas, the country's two major Malay political parties.
He said the cooperation would benefit Malays and Muslims while demonstrating that the unity agenda championed by Umno Youth could be translated into political action.
"Umno Youth is grateful and delighted by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's announcement of a political understanding between BN and Pas.
"The Melaka election will see the two largest Malay parties joining forces to ensure that the Malay-Muslim unity agenda becomes a reality for the sake of our people and religion.
"Thank you to the Umno president and Pas president for reaching this understanding," he said when contacted today.
Earlier, Zahid, who is also Umno president, confirmed that negotiations with Pas for the Melaka election had been finalised.
He announced that BN would contest 21 state assembly seats, while Pas and its allies would contest the remaining seven.
The agreement provides greater clarity on the two sides' electoral strategies and allows them to coordinate their campaigns to avoid contesting against each other.
BN is scheduled to announce its candidates on Oct 24 at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), while Pas is expected to unveil its candidates next week.
Umno Youth has previously called for Malay-Muslim political unity to prevent the fragmentation of electoral support, particularly in elections involving several competing parties.
Akmal has consistently championed the unity agenda as a means of strengthening Malay-Muslim political representation, including through cooperation between parties with shared political aspirations.

Title: 13,072 doctor posts vacant as of June
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 13,072 doctor posts in the Health Ministry were vacant as of June 30, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said.
Of the vacancies, 1,660 were for specialist medical officers, while the remaining 11,412 were for non-specialist medical officers.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said the Health Ministry recorded 3,510 resignations among permanent and contract medical officers between 2024 and 2026.
Of the total, 1,252 were permanent medical officers, while the remaining 2,258 were contract medical officers.
He said the ministry also recorded eight medical specialists who resigned or migrated overseas.
He added the resignations were out of a total of 14,064 medical officers appointed on a permanent basis and 9,847 on a contract basis by the ministry during the period.
Based on ministry records, Dzulkefly said the main reason for resignations was employment in the private sector, accounting for 51.4 per cent of cases.
"Personal reasons accounted for 36.8 per cent, followed by service with statutory bodies (4.5 per cent), working or residing overseas (2.9 per cent), health problems (2.6 per cent), furthering studies (1.5 per cent) and opening their own clinics (0.3 per cent)," he said in a written parliamentary reply to a question from V Ganabatirau (PH-Klang).
Ganabatirau had sought information on doctors resigning or migrating overseas, vacancies, specialist shortages, waiting times for housemanship placements and the effectiveness of measures to retain doctors.
Among the immediate measures to address the issue, he said a task force established by the Public Service Department in April was examining staffing issues.
"The ministry had also been given greater authority to manage and distribute approved positions to expedite recruitment."
In a separate development, Dzulkefly said six government hospitals had met the target of treating at least 70 per cent of non-emergency patients within two hours, compared with previous average waiting times of between four and six hours.
In a reply to Datuk Dr Zulkafperi Hanapi (Ind-Tanjong Karang), he said Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital in Ipoh recorded the highest performance, with 98.61 per cent of patients in the green zone receiving treatment within the two-hour target.
Ampang Hospital ranked second at 88.78 per cent, followed by Selayang Hospital at 74.1 per cent, Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Baru at 73.2 per cent, Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital in Klang at 72.2 per cent and Kuala Lumpur Hospital at 71.8 per cent.
"Patient attendance at the six major hospitals also fell by nine per cent after selected government health clinics extended their operating hours," Dzulkefly said.
He said the clinics now operate until 9pm on weekdays and from 8am to 1pm on weekends and public holidays.
"This measure to divert minor cases to health clinics has demonstrated an immediate impact, recording a reduction in physical patient attendance," he said.

Title: Tesla profits fall on higher spending as 'Elon Inc.' talk builds
Article:
NEW YORK: Tesla reported lower third-quarter profits Wednesday as near-trillionaire Elon Musk's electric vehicle maker ramped up huge investments in artificial intelligence and other envelope-pushing technologies.
Besides marginally lower car sales, Tesla saw a drop in revenues from regulatory credits and energy and storage, while spending on research and development more than doubled as the company engages in a spending binge on AI, robotics and autonomous transport.
The earnings were arguably upstaged by Musk's disclosure Tuesday that special committees of independent directors at both SpaceX and Tesla have been set up to discuss a merger of the two companies. Musk, who leads both companies, declined to offer further details Wednesday.
The potential merger – which some have dubbed "Elon Inc." – boosted shares of both companies on Wednesday, lifting Musk's wealth back near US$1 trillion at US$989 billion, according to Forbes' real-time billionaires index.
In the third quarter, Tesla reported profits of US$787 million, down 42.7 per cent from the year-ago period. Revenues were essentially flat at US$28 billion.
Analysts had been cautious about Tesla's latest results heading into Wednesday's release.
While third-quarter auto sales topped estimates, due in part to an uptick in European markets amid high gasoline prices, better sales have not always translated to Tesla's bottom line.
The company has faced questions about the rollout of Tesla's robotaxi venture that has progressed much more slowly than hoped.
Musk has repeatedly made overly rosy forecasts about self-driving technology, as in 2019 when he predicted there would be more than a million robotaxis the following year.
In Texas, where Tesla has focused its robotaxi launch, there are currently about 800 robotaxis, according to FSD Database.
Tesla's release highlighted the September 3 launch of robotaxi service in Austin and said "cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew eightfold quarter over quarter."
Company officials said Wednesday that if the current pace of robotaxi growth continues, the venture could be meaningful financially as early as next year. The ramp-up is guided by a strong desire to avoid safety problems, company officials said.
For much of this year, Tesla has also encountered scrutiny over swelling capital spending to fund ambitious programs in artificial intelligence, robotics and autonomous driving.
Capital spending more than doubled in the third quarter to US$4.7 billion, but the company lowered its capital spending plans compared with earlier in the year.
Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja, who in July had projected 2026 spending of more than US$25 billion, said Wednesday the company expects to spend US$20 billion, adding that the company managed "our capital deployment efficiently."
That is still more than double Tesla's 2025 capital budget of US$8.5 billion.
Besides robotaxi and AI, Tesla is heavily investing in Musk's "Optimus" humanoid robots as well as the buildout jointly with SpaceX of a large chip factory in Austin.
The chip factory, called Terafab, was the object of some of Musk's most effusive and self-boosting language on Wednesday.
"Terafab I think will be the most valuable building in the world, and will probably have an economic value that will place it in the top 20 of countries," he said.
Musk is also eyeing auto growth, projecting production of five million in 2030 compared with 1.7 million in 2025.
"After many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth," Musk said.
- Looming SpaceX merger? -
But questions about Tesla's future loomed larger with talk of the potential SpaceX tie-up. The companies have a combined equity value of more than US$3.5 trillion.
"We think it's a matter of when, not if" the two companies combine, said CFRA Research equity analyst Garrett Nelson.
"That's the whole issue," Nelson said of a potential megadeal. "Tesla as we know it today may not exist in six to 12 months."
On SpaceX's conference call Tuesday night, Musk said the committees have not agreed on the terms of any deal and there is no guarantee they will.
Musk said the two companies could gain from working together on AI software, chip design, robotics and space-based computing.
Talk of the deal heaps additional attention on Musk as the billionaire's latest cash infusion into US political elections fuels fresh criticism. Musk has steered at least US$276 million to allies of President Donald Trump in the Republican Party.
Musk is also under scrutiny over a report he ordered a reduction in Starshield telecom services for Ukraine, adding to pressure on the country at the same time Trump has criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and called for him to be replaced.
Shares of Tesla initially rose in after-hours trading, but were down 3.3 percent near 0050 GMT.

Title: MIDA's RM305bil green push puts local firms in the spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is targeting RM305 billion in green investments by 2030, with a stronger emphasis on ensuring local companies capture a bigger share of the opportunities through higher-value contracts, technology transfer and skilled job creation.
Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) deputy chief executive officer (Investment Development) Zuaida Abdullah said Malaysia had recorded RM45.8 billion in green investments to date, including RM12.5 billion in the renewable energy (RE) sector.
Between 2023 and 2025, MIDA approved nearly RM10 billion in renewable energy investments spanning solar, mini-hydro and bioenergy projects, underscoring the country's efforts to expand its clean energy capacity.
Investment momentum remained strong in the first half of 2026, with Malaysia approving RM218.5 billion in investments expected to generate more than 99,000 jobs.
However, Zuaida said attracting capital alone was insufficient, with the broader priority being to ensure investments generate lasting economic benefits by strengthening domestic supply chains, developing local expertise and creating quality employment.
She said MIDA was shifting towards an outcome-based approach to investment promotion, particularly through the new manufacturing sector incentive framework, which rewards companies for developing local suppliers, facilitating technology transfer and creating quality jobs.
The approach is intended to ensure foreign and domestic investments contribute more meaningfully to Malaysia's industrial capabilities rather than merely adding to headline investment figures, she told Bernama in an exclusive interview.
Olive Tree Property Consultants chief executive officer Samuel Tan said Malaysia's ability to translate its green investment ambitions into tangible economic gains would depend on how effectively local businesses were integrated into the renewable energy supply chain.
He told Business Times that greater domestic participation would help Malaysian companies build technical expertise, secure higher-value contracts and capture a larger share of the economic benefits as demand for green technologies and infrastructure expanded.
At the Greentech & Eco Products Exhibition & Conference Malaysia (IGEM) 2026, held from Oct 7 to 9, MIDA targeted RM4 billion in potential investments in the renewable energy sector.
Zuaida said Malaysia needed to prioritise domestic companies and local talent as demand for RE infrastructure expanded, supported by stable policies, reliable suppliers and a skilled workforce.
Major project owners, including TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd and TNB Renewables Sdn Bhd, play a strategic role in driving project development, while engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) contractors coordinate procurement, installation and testing.
These contractors also help identify qualified local vendors for components such as solar photovoltaic modules, inverters, mounting structures and cables, creating opportunities for Malaysian suppliers to participate in the renewable energy value chain.
Zuaida said that MIDA was actively working to connect local companies with major project developers by assisting domestic businesses in meeting the necessary technical standards and qualification requirements to secure contracts.
The initiative is particularly relevant to the sixth cycle of the Large-Scale Solar (LSS6) programme, which incorporates battery energy storage systems (BESS) with a total capacity of 2,650 megawatts.
Under the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry's policy, bidders using locally manufactured solar photovoltaic modules are given priority during the competitive evaluation process, providing an avenue for domestic manufacturers to strengthen their position in the growing clean energy market.
The government's latest green energy initiatives under Budget 2027 are expected to further expand investment opportunities across the sector.
MIDA welcomed the measures announced by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, including a RM1.5 billion investment to install solar systems at government buildings.
A dedicated 150-megawatt allocation under LSS6 has also been reserved for Bumiputera companies, supporting broader participation in the green economy.
Meanwhile, Tenaga Nasional Bhd plans to invest RM15 billion to strengthen the national electricity grid, while UEM Lestra is planning a RM1 billion energy storage system project at Kuala Lumpur International Airport.
UEM Lestra is also planning a one-gigawatt hybrid energy project in Johor, adding to the pipeline of large-scale renewable energy developments.
MIDA also welcomed the RM1 billion Climate Fund announced by Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) (KWAP), which will be dedicated entirely to green projects.
On the incentives front, the government has extended and enhanced the Green Investment Tax Allowance (GITA), offering investment tax allowances of up to 100 per cent until Dec 31, 2030.
The incentive is aimed at accelerating investment in renewable energy, decarbonisation and green technologies by encouraging businesses to adopt cleaner and more sustainable practices.
Tan said consistent policy support, effective investment incentives and continued infrastructure development would be important in sustaining Malaysia's green investment momentum and enabling local companies to participate more competitively in the transition.
Ultimately, he said the success of the country's green investment drive should be measured not only by the amount of capital attracted, but also by its ability to develop competitive Malaysian businesses, strengthen domestic industrial capabilities and retain more economic value within the country.

Title: Jobs over cost of living top concern among Perak residents
Article:
IPOH: Employment opportunities have overtaken the cost of living as the main concern among Perak residents, according to a survey by Institut Darul Ridzuan (IDR).
The shift in public priorities could reflect changing expectations of the state government's efforts to improve livelihoods under the Perak Sejahtera 2030 development agenda.
IDR chief executive officer Dr Zulqarnain Mohamad said the previous year's survey had identified cost of living as the main concern among respondents.
He said the latest findings suggested that residents were now placing greater emphasis on employment opportunities.
"Last year, the main concern was the cost of living. However, I believe the state government has introduced various initiatives, including Pasar Sejahtera Rakyat, which have helped the people.
"These efforts appear to have had a positive impact, with residents recognising the state government's initiatives.
"The survey also found that 66.4 per cent of respondents considered their monthly income sufficient, while 58.7 per cent said they could set aside money for emergency savings," he said.
He told reporters this after organising a dinner with Perak media practitioner at a hotel here last night. Also present was Perak Association of Media Practitioners president Sayed Mohd Hesham Syed Idris.
Zulqarnain said the findings were encouraging, although the survey did not establish the actual amount respondents had saved.
"We did not ask respondents about the exact amount of their emergency savings, so we cannot determine how much they had put aside," he said.
He said the survey also assessed residents' psychological capital, which measured their confidence and outlook for the future.
"The index recorded a score of 3.9 out of five, equivalent to 78 per cent," he added.
He said the findings indicated that residents were confident the state government could help improve their standard of living and overall well-being.
"Public confidence is important as it motivates us to work harder to improve the standard of living and socio-economic well-being of the people of Perak.
"However, we must continue working hard to ensure that this confidence translates into tangible improvements," he said.
IDR is an independent, non-profit think tank devoted to socio-economic research and development for the state government.
Meanwhile, he said IDR will hold its Perak Economic Outlook programme on Nov 16 to discuss the state's economic ecosystem, future direction and strategies to attract investment.
Zulqarnain said the programme would be among the institute's major initiatives this year.
"IDR will also hold its third Intellectual Discourse session of the year, focusing on ageing in Perak, which has one of the country's highest proportions of senior citizens," he added.

Title: Meta sued in Australia class action over alleged social media harm to children
Article:
SYDNEY: A class action lawsuit has been filed in an Australian court against Meta Platforms' Facebook and Instagram, alleging that the social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them hooked through algorithms.
The lawsuit, filed in the Federal Court of Australia, the country's second-highest court, by law firm MinterEllison this month, could be the first in Australia to hold social media responsible for harming its users, particularly children and teenagers.
The class action has been filed on behalf of eight plaintiffs, who allege they were harmed by Meta while they were under 18 and are seeking compensation.
Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In a suppression order on Monday, the court prohibited the reporting of any information that could reveal the identities of the applicants or the contents of the statement of claim.
Meta agreed in August to pay US$18 billion to settle claims brought by nearly all US states that it had designed social media to addict children.
The lawsuit comes amid rising tensions between Australia and Big Tech following a world-first ban on social media for children under 16 and newly proposed rules that could allow users to switch off algorithm-driven content in their feeds.

Title: Unhealthy air quality hits 16 areas nationwide, Nilai worst affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 16 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 8am today.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the affected areas were in Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Selangor, Johor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Negri Sembilan recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading nationwide, with Nilai registering 162, followed by Seremban (156) and Port Dickson (151).
Melaka also registered unhealthy readings, with Bukit Rambai recording 160, Bandaraya Melaka (148) and Alor Gajah (101).
Selangor saw five areas affected, led by Klang (156), Johan Setia (155), Petaling Jaya (153), Shah Alam (152) and Banting (136).
Johor's affected locations were Tangkak (153) and Pasir Gudang (109).
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur recorded unhealthy readings in Batu Muda (152) and Cheras (143), while Putrajaya registered 141.
APIMS data also showed that 49 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings.
Three areas recorded good air quality, namely Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (48), Kimanis (39) and Limbang (35).
API readings of 0 to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and readings above 300 as hazardous.

Title: Ringgit opens higher vs US dollar, major currencies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and most major currencies on Thursday as the greenback remained under pressure ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
At 8am, the ringgit was 4.0780/0835 against the greenback compared with Wednesday's close of 4.0790/0825.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment remains cautious ahead of next week's FOMC meeting, with investors closely monitoring inflation.
He also said crude oil prices rose after the latest attack on a Saudi oil field, with Brent crude currently hovering around US$108 per barrel.
Mohd Afzanizam added that US crude oil inventories fell by 3.06 million barrels in the week of Oct 16, which may suggest that the US government is attempting to stabilise their fuel prices.
"All in all, market sentiment remains cautious as the FOMC meeting next week will be closely monitored, especially on their stance towards inflation. As such, the ringgit will continue to trade in range today," he told Bernama.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened versus the Japanese yen to 2.5784/5820 from 2.5790/5814 at Wednesday's close and gained against the British pound to 5.4621/4694 from 5.4642/4689.
However, the local note edged down vis-a-vis the euro to 4.5812/5874 from 4.5770/5810
The ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
It gained vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.43/6.45 from 6.44/6.45 at Wednesday's close but was flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 226.2/226.7.
The local note eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.1929/1975 from 3.1917/1947 and fell versus the Thai baht to 12.1387/1623 from 12.1287/1434 at yesterday's close.

Title: Oil rises as US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid escalating tensions
Article:
NEW YORK: Oil prices rose on Thursday as more attacks by the Houthis in Saudi Arabia prompted the United States to order some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the Kingdom.
Brent crude futures rose US$1.29, or 1.2 per cent, to US$110.11 a barrel at 00:34 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 97 cents, or 1 per cent, to US$98.12. Brent had settled largely unchanged on Wednesday, while WTI had eased 67 cents.
The US State Department plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis struck several targets on Wednesday with at least one person killed and eight more wounded at a civilian airport in Dammam, and two people killed in a drone attack on a Saudi oil field.
Explosions were also heard in Sirik in southern Iran, Iranian media reported on Wednesday, saying the nature and origin of the explosions were unknown.
On Wednesday, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself and President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.
There were at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks, Kpler data showed, while LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, reaching into the Gulf of Oman and jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers supporting regional loadings.
Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday for talks on ending the war in Ukraine amid Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he supported the talks and hoped they would start as soon as possible.
US crude stocks fell by 3.06 million barrels to 412.5 million barrels last week, the US Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for an 820,000-barrel draw.
Distillate stockpiles, which include diesel and heating oil, rose 1.68 million barrels in the week to 104.3 million barrels, versus expectations for a 1.16 million-barrel drop, EIA data showed.
The Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the 1-million-barrel US emergency heating oil reserve, the Department of Energy said on Wednesday, seeking to contain prices that have surged on diesel shortages due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

Title: At 18, Leesya weighs just 14kg, relies on mother for every need
Article:
PETALING JAYA: At 18, Khalisah Damia Abd Kadim, known as Leesya, weighs just 14kg and is bedridden due to cerebral palsy.
Unlike other teenagers her age, Leesya is unable to walk or crawl and can utter only two words: "ayah" (father) and "ibu" (mother).
She also has scoliosis, a condition involving an abnormal curvature of the spine.
Her mother, Siti Robaah Mohd Munaf, 56, said Leesya, the youngest of six siblings, had appeared healthy at birth.
"Everything changed when Leesya developed jaundice, with her bilirubin levels rising sharply on the fifth day after she was born.
"My husband and I took her to a clinic, where the doctor gave us a referral letter and asked us to take her to hospital.
"Following further examinations, doctors suspected that Leesya had cerebral palsy, and she was subsequently registered as a person with disabilities under the physical disability category," she said when met at her home in Kampung Lindungan here.
Siti Robaah admitted that she initially struggled to accept her daughter's condition, having hoped that Leesya would grow up without health problems.
"It took me some time to come to terms with what had happened. I cried, but eventually accepted it because I believe this is what God has decreed.
"Since Leesya was born, I have never heard anyone say anything hurtful about her. Everyone, including our relatives and close friends, has accepted her.
"However, Leesya is not like other teenagers her age. Many people think she is still a baby or a young child because of her small frame. Her growth began slowing down and appeared to become stunted when she was 13," she said.
Siti Robaah, a housewife, said she spent most of her time caring for Leesya and attending to her daily needs.
"My daily routine involves giving Leesya special formula milk every four hours, six times a day.
"I also have to put her on breathing support and help remove mucus from her airways using a machine at home.
"Caring for a child like this requires a great deal of patience because when Leesya becomes distressed, she vomits. She has also been admitted to hospital many times, usually because of fever or infections," she said.
Siti Robaah, who is also a stroke survivor, said she would continue caring for her daughter for as long as she lived.
"I have already reminded my husband and other children to look after Leesya if I pass away before her," she said.
Meanwhile, Leesya's brother, Mohamad Zamrin Abd Kadim, 23, who is pursuing a bachelor's degree in Computer Software Engineering in Multimedia at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, said he helped care for his sister whenever he had free time despite undergoing industrial training.
"At first, I did not really understand her condition, but as I grew older, I began to understand and realise my responsibilities.
"Whatever happens, I will take turns caring for my sister because I will never leave her alone," he said.
Mohamad Zamrin has also worked as a delivery rider for the past three years to help pay his university fees and ease his family's financial burden.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nasdaq leads Wall Street gains as SpaceX, Super Micro boost AI sentiment
Article:
NEW YORK: The tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close on Wednesday after quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer improved investor appetite for artificial intelligence-related stocks while weakness in communication services stocks capped gains.
SpaceX shares finished up 7.8 per cent after Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm posted its first profit as a public company. Musk said, following the report, that a merger of SpaceX and Tesla would be "a good idea," also boosting Tesla shares.
Elsewhere in earnings, Super Micro shares jumped 9.6 per cent and it was among the S&P 500's top gainers after the AI server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. The report also benefited peers HPE, which rose 3.7 per cent, and Dell, which rose 5.3 per cent.
The reports provided some reassurance to investors who have been worried about the sustainability of massive spending on AI buildouts and their profitability. The technology sector was hammered last week by a selloff in AI-linked stocks, with data center operator CoreWeave at the center of the storm.
The SpaceX news "pushes back on some of the investor worries" about AI along with some help from Super Micro, according to Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones.
Kourkafas said the reports will not "answer all the questions investors have on returns on AI investments, but it's a good start."
As a result, the S&P 500 Information Technology index finished up 1.6 per cent, the biggest gainer among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors.
"It's really a positive technology story for almost anyone that is somewhat involved in the artificial intelligence ecosystem," said Marc Dizard, chief investment officer at Huntington Bank.
"The technology market reaction has been a reaffirmation that the artificial intelligence trade is still intact," he added.
However, Dizard said sentiment can quickly shift around AI and that investors will seek reaffirmation when they monitor earnings reports from other companies.
Shares in Meta rose 3 per cent in late trading after it released its quarterly results following the regular session's close. After finishing up 3.4 per cent in the regular session, Tesla shares rose another 1.6 per cent following its report, which was also issued after the close.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 360.21 points, or 0.69 per cent, to 52,856.09, the S&P 500 gained 44.60 points, or 0.58 per cent, to 7,757.17 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 278.04 points, or 1.05 per cent, to 26,702.86.
Within technology, one of the strongest areas was chips with a 2 per cent rally in the Philadelphia Semiconductor index, which has had a volatile month so far including an eight-session selloff.
Gains in the benchmark S&P 500 were limited however by a 1.3 per cent decline in communication services stocks. The biggest losers included telecom operators such as AT&T, which sank 6.5 per cent even as it beat third-quarter revenue and profit expectations.
The SpaceX results, along with a recent wireless spectrum purchase, fanned fears that it could become a formidable competitor in telecoms, according to Dizard. T-Mobile US shares fell 2.5 per cent and Verizon Communications lost 2.2 per cent.
Also in communications services, Netflix shares sank 5.3 per cent after the video streaming company issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for its fourth-quarter profit. Google's parent Alphabet also declined 1.6 per cent.
Abbott Laboratories shares dropped 1.9 per cent after the medical device maker cut its 2026 sales growth forecast.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.37-to-1 ratio on the NYSE where there were 131 new highs and 221 new lows. On the Nasdaq, 2,690 stocks rose and 2,068 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.3-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 26 new 52-week highs and 3 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 53 new highs and 216 new lows.
On US exchanges roughly 16.11 billion shares changed hands compared with the 17.10 billion average for the last 20 sessions.

Title: Four injured in BMW-oil tanker crash on Penang Bridge
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Four people were injured when a BMW collided with an oil tanker on the Penang Bridge.
The accident occurred at Km3.4 of the bridge's mainland-to-island bound carriageway at 12.13am.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the four occupants of the BMW had been taken to hospital by members of the public before firefighters arrived.
The 53-year-old tanker driver escaped unhurt.
"We received the emergency call at 12.13am and rushed to the scene," he said.
Twelve firefighters, supported by a fire and rescue vehicle and an emergency medical rescue services unit, were deployed to the scene.
Firefighters cleared debris to eliminate further hazards before ending the operation at 1.11am.
Police and PLUS personnel were also on hand to assist.
One of the injured was identified as a 44-year-old man, while the identities of the other three were not available.

Title: Teen accused of injuring Kuching teacher no longer active student
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The teenager accused of injuring a teacher at an international school in Kuching, Sarawak, this morning is no longer an active student at the institution.
In a statement yesterday, the school said the student was in police custody pending further investigations.
It said the case was being investigated by police and the school would continue to cooperate fully with the relevant authorities.
"The injured teacher was taken to hospital by ambulance for treatment. At this stage, the teacher is recovering and has not sustained critical injuries.
"The school deeply appreciates our teacher's courage and composure during the incident and wishes them a smooth recovery," the statement said.
The school said it had immediately activated its emergency response protocols following the incident, with teachers and staff promptly alerting the police and ambulance services.
Students in the affected classroom were safely evacuated, and no other injuries were reported.
As a precaution, classes were dismissed early on police advice, while parents were promptly notified to pick up their children.
The school confirmed that it would reopen on Thursday, subject to clearance from the relevant authorities.
It said safety protocols were being reviewed and security measures strengthened.
"Effective immediately, three auxiliary police personnel will be stationed on the school grounds, and appropriate security checks will be conducted at entry points.
"The school is also reviewing more comprehensive long-term security measures for the campus," it said.
The school added that its senior leadership team would hold a student assembly to explain the incident, reassure students and address their concerns, including by providing counselling support.
It urged the public not to speculate, circulate unverified information or spread rumours that could interfere with investigations.
"We also ask that the privacy of those involved be respected while the relevant authorities carry out their duties," it said.
The school also expressed its appreciation to teachers, staff and students for their swift response and professionalism in helping safeguard the school community during the incident.
Earlier, media reports said a 16-year-old male student at an international school had recorded a video before a teacher attempted to wrest a sharp object from him this morning.
A video purportedly recorded by the student before the incident has also circulated on social media, drawing widespread attention. However, the contents and actual purpose of the recording remain under investigation.

Title: Rational investing amidst international conflicts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: International conflicts, geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty have made stock investing increasingly challenging. Wars, trade disputes, sanctions, disruptions to energy supplies and strained relations between major powers can unsettle financial markets and undermine investor confidence. Share prices may fluctuate sharply, sometimes in response to events that have little immediate impact on the underlying businesses.
In such turbulent times, investors must recognise that successful investing is not about predicting every geopolitical development. It is about making rational decisions, managing risks and remaining focused on the long-term fundamentals of the businesses in which they invest.
Understand the Difference Between Uncertainty and Permanent Damage
Stock markets dislike uncertainty. When international conflicts escalate, investors may sell shares out of fear that economic growth will slow, inflation will rise or corporate earnings will deteriorate. However, a falling share price does not automatically mean that a company's intrinsic value has declined by the same proportion.
Investors must distinguish between temporary market anxiety and permanent damage to a business. A company with strong finances, recurring revenues, a competitive advantage and resilient demand may withstand geopolitical turbulence better than its share price initially suggests.
Conversely, some businesses may suffer lasting consequences from prolonged conflicts, particularly those dependent on disrupted supply chains, vulnerable export markets or volatile commodity prices. The important question is not simply whether a share price has fallen, but whether the company's long-term earnings power and financial position have fundamentally changed.
Focus on Financial Strength and Cash Flow
During uncertain periods, financially sound businesses become particularly valuable. Investors should examine a company's debt levels, cash reserves, operating cash flow, interest obligations and ability to generate profits under adverse conditions.
Companies carrying excessive debt may struggle when borrowing costs rise or revenues decline. Businesses with weak cash generation may be forced to borrow, raise new capital or cut dividends at precisely the wrong time.
Cash flow deserves special attention because reported accounting profits do not necessarily translate into cash available to meet obligations. A company that consistently converts earnings into cash is generally better positioned to survive economic shocks, maintain operations and seize opportunities when weaker competitors retreat.
Maintain a Margin of Safety
Uncertainty increases the importance of valuation discipline. Even an excellent company can become a poor investment if purchased at an excessive price.
A margin of safety means buying a share at a meaningful discount to a conservatively estimated intrinsic value. This provides some protection against errors in analysis, unexpected economic developments and further deterioration in business conditions.
When markets fall, investors should not assume that every declining share has become cheap. Some prices fall because the market is excessively pessimistic; others fall because the underlying business is genuinely deteriorating. Careful analysis is essential to distinguish between these situations.
Diversify Without Diluting Investment Quality
Diversification helps reduce the damage caused by an adverse event affecting a particular company, industry or country. Investors should avoid excessive concentration in businesses exposed to the same geopolitical risks.
For Malaysian investors, this means considering exposure to domestic demand, export markets, currencies, commodity prices and international supply chains. Different industries respond differently to global disruptions. Energy producers may benefit from higher oil prices, while transport companies and energy-intensive manufacturers may face rising costs.
Nevertheless, diversification should not become an excuse to own businesses that are poorly understood or financially weak. A portfolio of carefully selected, financially resilient companies is preferable to indiscriminate diversification.
Keep Cash and Avoid Emotional Decisions
Holding some cash can provide flexibility during periods of uncertainty. It also allows investors to take advantage of attractive opportunities without being forced to sell existing investments at depressed prices.
However, holding excessive cash indefinitely has its own costs, including inflation and the potential loss of long-term investment returns. The appropriate allocation depends on investment objectives, time horizon, liquidity requirements and risk tolerance.
Investors should also avoid excessive leverage and margin financing. Borrowing to invest magnifies losses and may force the sale of shares during market declines, leaving investors unable to benefit from a subsequent recovery.
Adopt a Long-Term Perspective
History demonstrates that markets have endured wars, recessions, financial crises and political upheavals. Although past recoveries do not guarantee future outcomes, businesses that remain competitive and financially sound can continue creating value despite a difficult external environment.
Long-term investors should review their holdings regularly, but not confuse activity with progress. If the fundamentals remain intact and the valuation remains reasonable, temporary volatility may be something to tolerate rather than fear.
Conclusion
In the final analysis, uncertainty is an unavoidable feature of investing. The greatest advantage an investor can possess is not the ability to predict the future, but the discipline to make sound decisions when the future is uncertain.

Title: Iskandar Malaysia's next test: Turning RM525bil investments into lasting economic gains
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Malaysia's next challenge is turning investment into sustainable growth, higher-value jobs and stronger local businesses, industry experts said.
The Johor economic corridor marks its 20th anniversary this year with RM525.26 billion in cumulative investments, surpassing its original RM383 billion target by RM142.26 billion.
Industry experts said the focus now is on building a more advanced industrial base, improving liveability and helping Malaysian companies secure a bigger role in regional and global supply chains.
Zerin Properties founder and chief executive officer Previndran Singhe said Iskandar Malaysia's investment performance reflected the sustained efforts of the Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) and the Johor government.
"This has been a long time coming, and I welcome it. When Iskandar was launched in 2006, plenty of people in our industry, myself included, wondered how long it would take to gain real traction, said Previndran who has more than 35 years of experience in the property industry,
"RM525 billion later, with over a million jobs created and household incomes more than doubled, the answer is clear. IRDA and the Johor government deserve the credit," he told Business Times.
However, he said the next phase would be more demanding, as attracting investment alone would not guarantee that Iskandar Malaysia became a compelling place to live, work and build businesses.
"Attracting capital is one thing. Building places people actually want to live in is another," he said.
Previndran said companies and skilled professionals increasingly considered quality of life alongside office costs, rental rates and other conventional investment factors when deciding where to establish operations or build careers.
A young engineer or regional executive choosing between Johor and another regional destination would also consider access to parks, cafés, cultural activities, reliable public transport and shorter commuting times, he said.
"Investors follow talent, and talent goes where life is good. Those everyday things matter more than any brochure," he said.
He said Iskandar Malaysia already had considerable advantages, including its waterfront, marinas, the historic character of Johor Bahru's old town, green spaces and a young population.
However, better public transport, more coordinated urban planning and stronger community amenities would be necessary to make the region more attractive to residents and investors over the long term.
The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is expected to transform cross-border mobility, but its benefits would depend partly on how effectively commuters could connect to destinations beyond the rail stations.
"The RTS Link will change how people move between Johor Baru and Singapore, but if you step off the train and the only way forward is a Grab or your own car, we have missed the point," Previndran said, calling for reliable bus services, a proper rapid transit network, and shaded walkways and cycling paths linking townships.
He also highlighted the need for closer coordination among local authorities, particularly in planning approvals, infrastructure delivery and township management.
More vibrant neighbourhoods, with independent cafés, bookshops, small businesses, weekend markets and cultural activities, could help give Johor Bahru a stronger urban identity and encourage more visitors from Singapore to spend time in the city beyond shopping and refuelling, he said.
Sustainability should also be incorporated into future development through greener buildings, more trees, improved drainage and inclusive communities designed to serve different generations.
"Iskandar has shown the world it can bring in investment. The next 20 years will be about making it a place people are proud to call home," he said.
Olive Tree Property Consultants founder and chief executive officer Samuel Tan said Iskandar Malaysia's next phase of growth would depend on how effectively it leveraged its strategic location and the complementary strengths of Johor and Singapore, particularly through the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
The JS-SEZ aims to strengthen economic integration between the two jurisdictions by combining Johor's land availability, industrial capacity, talent pool and competitive operating costs with Singapore's international capital, technology, business networks and access to global markets.
The zone attracted RM76.98 billion in approved investments in 2025, highlighting Johor's appeal as a complementary base for companies seeking to expand their regional operations.
Tan said the opportunity was significant, but realising its full potential would require close coordination between the two governments, particularly in infrastructure planning, energy security, workforce development and cross-border mobility.
Streamlined customs and immigration procedures, alongside stronger physical and digital connectivity, would also be essential to reducing operating costs and enabling businesses to move goods, people and services more efficiently across the border.
"The JS-SEZ creates a significant advantage by bringing together complementary strengths that no single jurisdiction could offer in isolation.
"This includes Johor's abundant land, established industrial capacity, growing talent pool and competitive operating expenses, alongside Singapore's global capital networks, technology, business services and access to international markets," he told Business Times.
The need to translate investment momentum into tangible economic outcomes is also reflected in the government's broader efforts to develop strategic industrial and logistics hubs.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat earlier this month, said Sedenak Nexus in the northern part of the JS-SEZ had the potential to attract RM12 billion in investments and create 45,000 jobs.
He also said the government would continue strengthening special border economic zones, with trade along the Bukit Kayu Hitam-Sadao corridor reaching RM27 billion in the first six months of this year.
One initiative is the development of the 49.37-hectare NCT InnoSphere as a heavy vehicle, engineering, maintenance and logistics hub serving industries in Kulim and Penang.
According to IRDA, Iskandar Malaysia has generated more than one million jobs and more than doubled average household incomes since its establishment.
However, with competition for investment intensifying across Asean, the region faces growing pressure to move beyond attracting capital and build a more productive economic ecosystem that generates skilled employment, strengthens domestic supply chains and enables Malaysian companies to capture a greater share of the value created.
IRDA said its next development phase would prioritise advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, modern logistics, and high-value financial and business services.
"Emphasis will be placed on increasing productivity and high-value economic activity, including advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, and logistics, as well as financial and business services," it said in a statement on Tuesday.
The authority said its strategy would extend beyond headline investment figures to encompass technology transfer, domestic business participation, local innovation and the ability of Malaysian enterprises to move up the global value chain.
Deputy Prime Minister II and Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said Iskandar Malaysia's next phase must be measured by the quality and sustainability of its economic gains, rather than investment figures alone.
Fadillah chaired the 36th IRDA Governing Council meeting on behalf of Anwar, alongside Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
"The next phase should be assessed not only by the total investment attracted but also by the quality of opportunities created, the strength of the economic ecosystem, and the long-term benefits that businesses and communities can enjoy," he said.
IRDA said land availability and competitive costs, once major considerations for investors, were no longer sufficient to guarantee competitiveness as businesses increasingly assessed infrastructure readiness, energy reliability, skilled labour availability and digital connectivity.
The efficiency of cross-border movement for goods and people, together with access to regional and international markets, had also become increasingly important in investment decisions.

Title: Explainer: Why is Sabah's Pan Borneo Highway lagging behind Sarawak's?
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The toll-free Pan Borneo Highway was envisioned as a major transport link connecting Sabah, Sarawak and Brunei. But more than a decade after its launch, progress in the two East Malaysian states has diverged sharply.
As of March 31, the Auditor General's Report 2/2026 found that Sarawak had completed 10 of its 11 work packages, with the remaining package, WP11, 99.9 per cent complete.
In Sabah, only four of the 35 work packages under Phase 1, which spans 706km, had been completed.
Of the
remaining packages
, nine were classified as sick projects, 13 were delayed and nine were ahead of schedule.
A total of RM10.547 billion of the RM11.153 billion allocated for Sabah's highway project had been spent, yet the project remains significantly behind schedule.
The completion deadline has since been extended to 2030 due to weaknesses in project planning.
Public Accounts Committee chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin has warned that the project risks remaining incomplete due to a
funding shortfall
unless the government approves additional allocations.
WHY IS SARAWAK'S PORTION PROGRESSING WELL?
In 2024, former Sabah Works Minister Datuk Shahelmey Yahya said Sarawak had arranged sukuk financing early to ensure sufficient funds for all its Pan Borneo Highway packages.
According to DanaInfra Nasional Berhad's website, the infrastructure financing entity was mandated in July 2015 to raise funds to part-finance Phase 1 of the Sarawak Pan Borneo Highway, with financing of up to RM13 billion backed by a government guarantee.
The financing programme was expanded to RM15.8 billion in May 2023 to meet the remaining construction funding requirements.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi also credited Building Information Modelling (BIM) technology with saving RM157 million and averting a potential
10-year delay
to the Sarawak project.
The MP for Kapit said the technology helped resolve more than 3,000 drawing errors during construction in 2016.
WHY IS SABAH'S PAN BORNEO HIGHWAY FACING DELAYS?
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister and Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said this year that the project had been affected by the
termination
of the previous project delivery partner (PDP) model in 2019.
The switch to the conventional implementation model left the project dependent on annual federal allocations.
Dr Gunsalam said most contractor appointments for the new packages were finalised only between February 2024 and January 2026, after the federal government reconsidered the implementation method.
Land acquisition has also held up construction, with the state government allowing landowners to appeal against compensation offers.
Shortages of bitumen, stone and manpower have also
contributed
to the delays.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan previously told Parliament that other
factors
included contractor performance, weather conditions, utility relocation, the Covid-19 pandemic and weaknesses in project governance.

Title: HRD Corp rolls out massive procedural overhaul [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   The Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) has tightened training grant approvals, stepped up programme verification and strengthened investment safeguards as part of a sweeping reform to address governance weaknesses and restore stakeholder confidence.
Its chief executive, Datuk Shamir Aziz, said the organisation has introduced stricter application requirements, as well as increased physical and digital checks on training programmes and overhauled procurement procedures following findings in the Auditor General's Report 2024.
Since June, training applications must be submitted at least 14 days before a programme begins, ending retrospective approvals and giving HRD Corp more time to scrutinise documents and ensure compliance.
The Auditor General's Report 2024 had flagged 62 levy applications worth RM1.68 million that were approved after training had taken place.
It also highlighted questionable applications involving repeated participant information and training facilities that did not correspond with approved specifications.
Shamir, who was appointed to the role in January, is at the heart of the sweeping reforms, which aims to close loopholes while ensuring employers can continue to access training support.
"I inherited a heavy ledger of broken trust. Entrusted with the levies of over 109,000 employers funding 5.4 million Malaysian workers, it is my promise to restore trust and integrity in HRD Corp," he said.
Since the 14-day advance application policy took effect, HRD Corp has received 137,460 applications under its HRD Corp Claimable Courses scheme for in-house training and public programmes, an increase of nearly 12 per cent over the same period last year.
However, the approval rate fell to 78.8 per cent from 93.1 per cent last year, which Shamir attributed to more rigorous screening under the reformed process.
"Retrospective training approvals are a thing of the past. All training sessions must now be applied for at least 14 days beforehand.
"This policy allows HRD Corp ample time to rigorously check paperwork and approve training in accordance with its procedures, leaving virtually no room for manipulation."
The manufacturing sector accounted for the largest share of approvals at 26 per cent, followed by wholesale and retail at 14 per cent, professional and technical services at 12 per cent and construction at eight per cent.
HRD Corp has also significantly increased checks to establish whether approved training programmes are actually conducted.
The agency verified 6,231 training programmes last year. Between June and September this year, it verified 19,322 sessions.
"That is roughly three times the previous year's total, achieved in just four months," said Shamir.
To address staffing limitations, more than 15,000 training sessions were verified digitally, while 3,500 underwent physical inspection.
Nonetheless, the agency aims to achieve 100 per cent verification of training programmes.
Shamir said HRD Corp was developing a system incorporating MyDigital ID, QR codes, geotagging and timestamps to verify attendance, with a pilot planned for next year and full implementation targeted for 2028.
FUNDS MANAGED WITH DISCIPLINE AND INTEGRITY
Despite the tighter controls, HRD Corp continued to disburse funds to employers, paying RM1.4 billion across 335,877 approved claims since January.
"This figure represents the 335,877 decisions by employers to invest in their people, and HRD Corp stood behind every one of them," Shamir said.
ACCOUNTABILITY AND INVESTMENT SAFEGUARDS
Shamir said internal reviews into four critical areas — the management of unutilised levies, the acquisition of Menara Ikhlas, investment management and the overdue RM14 million procurement of the New Core System — had led to action against its personnel.
Six senior officers were suspended from their positions this year and they are no longer with the organisation. Three of them were subsequently dismissed.
"Accountability is where reform begins, not where it ends. I was brought in to clean up HRD Corp and that is exactly what I intend to do. There will be no tolerance for failures of accountability.
"Every ringgit entrusted to us belongs to Malaysian employers and workers. We will ensure it is managed with the discipline and integrity they deserve," Shamir  said.
HRD Corp is also working to address concerns over investments made between 2020 and 2024, when part of its funds was invested in high-risk instruments without adequate safeguards.
Shamir said RM447.2 million had been recovered.
"The remaining exposure is down to RM396.3 million, or 8.6 per cent of total investment funds, and legal action to recover the rest is ongoing. This episode cannot repeat itself."
He said investments were permitted under the Human Resources Development Act 2001 and were necessary to sustain the organisation's operations and staff salaries.
"The four per cent service fee, event revenue and other income are simply insufficient to sustain HRD Corp's vast operations, especially to support three million training opportunities in 2027."
Moving forward, all investments must be backed by collateral equivalent to 110 per cent of the investment, excluding shares.
"Put simply, if an investment fails, we can claim assets worth more than we invested," Shamir said.
RAISED BY AUDITOR GENERAL ADDRESSED
Of the 10 issues raised in the Auditor General's Report 2024, four were resolved last year, five remain on the auditor general's dashboard for continued monitoring and one was being addressed.
HRD Corp also appointed five new board members in February, bringing expertise in retail, Islamic finance, manufacturing, export markets, energy and cooperatives.
Shamir said the board's diverse experience would strengthen checks and balances, protect public trust and support skills development among Malaysian workers.
PROCUREMENT OVERHAUL AND TRAINING PRIORITIES
The RM14 million New Core System, a digital platform procured by HRD Corp, had fallen years behind schedule and failed user-acceptance testing three times, prompting changes to procurement procedures.
Shamir said all procurement exercises now went through open tender and were assessed by three committees comprising members from different departments.
For smaller purchases, the lowest bid would no longer automatically prevail, with quality, delivery and value also taken into account.
Tender periods had also been extended from seven to 21 days in line with Finance Ministry guidelines.
"A fair process is not a favour we grant. It is an obligation we owe."
[[nid:1561048]]
TRAINING FRAMEWORK REVIEW
With the governance reforms underway, HRD Corp is also reviewing its training framework to better meet employers' needs and align skills development with industry requirements.
The organisation has engaged more than 500 employers, training providers and industry associations as it revises its Allowable Cost Matrix.
Consultations will continue until the end of the year and stakeholders are encouraged to provide feedback.
Training schemes are being regrouped around high-impact areas, with greater emphasis on professional certification to support Malaysia's target of having 35 per cent of its workforce classified as skilled by 2030.
HRD Corp is also working to make Continuing Professional Development points for professionals claimable under the revised framework.
"Our primary focus is our stakeholders, the employers and those who contribute to the fund. We want to know what employers need; they are our priority.
"We have a plan. We know it's not perfect, but we will keep striving for better," said Shamir.
Next year, HRD Corp aims to make company-sponsored educational degrees a claimable benefit from levy accounts.
To boost retention beyond just tax exemptions, employers will be able to use their levies as scholarships to upskill staff.
"We foresee that as soon as next year, job advertisements will prominently feature scholarships." he said.
PROFESSIONALISING THE CARE SECTOR
HRD Corp's expanded role in skills development will also include efforts to professionalise the caregiving sector and create opportunities for women and other groups seeking employment.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced a RM40 million allocation  for HRD Corp's Madani Professional Caregiver initiative under the 2027 Budget on Oct 9.
The programme aims to train
up to 8,000 people, including homemakers, housewives, school leavers, technical and vocational education and training  graduates and jobseekers.
Shamir said the initiative would recognise the skills required in caregiving and help establish clearer standards in  the sector.
"Caring for the elderly or disabled is highly skilled, demanding work. It deserves proper training, clear standards, and fair wages."
He thanked the prime minister and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan for their support, as well as HRD Corp employees for their contributions to the reform process.
"HRD Corp belongs to the employers and workers of Malaysia. We hold every ringgit in trust for them.
"We have not finished keeping that promise, but we are keeping it, day by day, claim by claim, ringgit by ringgit.
"The work will continue."

Title: Washington orders US embassy staff, families to leave Saudi Arabia
Article:
WASHINGTON: The United States has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a social media post explaining the measure.
"The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority," he added.
A diplomatic source in the Middle East told AFP that some families of US embassy personnel were also being withdrawn from the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, but Pigott stressed that Wednesday's order applied only to the departure of non-emergency embassy staff and their families in Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia has come under near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis this month, including a strike on Riyadh's international airport that was the kingdom's deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates.
On Wednesday, the Saudi energy ministry said falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility had killed two people and injured two others.
"The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others," the ministry said in a statement.
It did not say who launched the drone aimed at the Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported intercepting six drones.
One person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, aviation officials said.
In June, a four-year truce in Yemen's civil war collapsed, reviving a conflict that dates back to 2014. The Saudi-led coalition has backed the internationally recognised government since 2015.
Iran explosions
The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran in late February, and again in July before US President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes.
Late on Wednesday, Iranian state media reported the sound of explosions in the southern Hormozgan province overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, breaking a spell of relative calm.
"A few minutes ago, the sound of several explosions was heard in the Karpan area of Sirik, in Hormozgan Province," the official IRNA news agency said.
It added that "local sources have not yet disclosed the nature of these explosions".
In late February, the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran, killing the country's supreme leader and senior military commanders.
Iran has attempted to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, demanding that all ships seek its authorisation to cross. In peacetime, the strategic waterway carried around a fifth of the world's oil supplies.
In retaliation, the United States has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and ships.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sisi says Egypt to 'defend Saudi territory' and will not attack Yemen
Article:
CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo's proposed military support for Riyadh was intended to "defend Saudi territory and does not include an attack on Yemen".
At a government event titled Egypt Forum 2026, Sisi said: "We are talking about defending the land and borders of the kingdom."
"The situation cannot bear any further instability in other countries. We want to restore the countries that have lost their stability," he added.
Sisi on Saturday asked parliament to authorise support for Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis, "if requested".
The parliament, which is packed with supporters of the president, has since held two rare closed-door sessions before postponing deliberations until next week.
Following the morning event at which Sisi made the speech, which was reported later, a high-level Egyptian delegation visited Riyadh, the kingdom's state news agency reported.
Egypt's top diplomat Badr Abdelatty and spy chief Hassan Rashad delivered a letter from Sisi to Saudi Arabia's de facto ruler, Mohammed bin Salman, the Saudi Press Agency said.
The contents of the message were not reported.
In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have reached an unprecedented scale, forcing Riyadh to shut its main airport and postpone a major investment conference.
A Houthi maritime blockade is also threatening oil exports from the kingdom, the world's biggest crude exporter.
Saudi Arabia has since rallied support from its allies. French President Emmanuel Macron, on a surprise "solidarity" visit to the kingdom on Wednesday, said French troops would help shield the key oil terminal of Yanbu on the Red Sea.
The day before, the UK government announced it would deploy British fighter jets to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against increasing attacks.
Egypt's tightrope
A handful of dissenting voices in Egypt's parliament have demanded "specific objectives and clear information" on any possible deployment, as well as an assessment of the "potential risks to the lives of our soldiers".
Direct military involvement is unpopular in the Arab world's most populous nation, while memories remain of its last disastrous deployment in Yemen in the 1960s, when thousands of soldiers were killed fighting in the North Yemen civil war.
That mission, under President Gamal Abdel Nasser, was later compared with the US war in Vietnam.
Riyadh is one of Cairo's strongest allies and a key financial backer of Sisi's administration since the former army chief ousted Islamist president Mohammed Morsi in 2013.
In his speech on Saturday, Sisi said it was "inconceivable" for Cairo to stand by as Riyadh's security and stability were threatened, given the unconditional support the kingdom had provided Egypt in the early days of his administration.
Egypt joined the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen in 2015, contributing naval and air forces and deploying warships to the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait.
But over the past decade, it has adopted an increasingly cautious foreign policy, prioritising its own national security.
It has positioned itself as a regional mediator, maintaining channels across conflict lines, including with Hamas, Israel and Iran.
On Wednesday, Abdelatty again said Egypt's foreign policy was defined by "wisdom and strategic balance".
This week, Abdelatty has been in contact with Iran's top diplomat, Abbas Araghchi, who has said that Egypt's potential involvement would make the situation "more difficult".
"Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict," Araghchi said in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday.
Throughout this year, as its Gulf allies have come under attack in the war between Iran and the US, Cairo has repeatedly urged caution.
The Arab world's largest military did not issue a response even when its own Damietta port was struck by an unidentified drone in July.
It has not joined the Mecca defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan in August, which experts said was intended to preserve its strategic autonomy.
Besides its close alliance with the kingdom, Egypt also has its own economic woes to consider.
Along with Saudi Arabia, Egypt has been hit hard by disruptions through Bab al-Mandab, the southern gateway to the Suez Canal, whose revenues have yet to recover since Houthi attacks began in 2023.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: French fighter jet crashes during training, two killed
Article:
PARIS: A French Mirage 2000D fighter jet crashed in northeastern France during a training flight, killing both crew members, officials said on Wednesday.
The plane went down at 2100 GMT on Tuesday near its air base on the outskirts of the city of Nancy.
During a press briefing in Doha, where he is on a visit, President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday expressed "the nation's condolences".
Neither the pilot, aged 27, nor his 44-year-old navigator had time to eject before the aircraft hit the ground, Metz prosecutor David Touvet told AFP on Wednesday evening.
The motors from the ejection seats were found at the crash site.
"Given the violence of the impact, no element of the investigation allows us to think that either of the two crew members will be found alive," Touvet said.
DNA analyses, which could take several weeks, will have to be carried out to identify the victims, he said.
The crew comprised "a highly experienced navigator and a young pilot who arrived at the base with all the prerequisites and qualifications needed to fly" a Mirage, air base commander Ludovic Humbert said.
"The pilot had 450 flight hours," Colonel David Pappalardo, spokesman for the Air and Space Force (AAE), told reporters in Paris.
He was "in the process of qualifying as an operational combat pilot", he said.
"At the end of the tactical phase of the training exercise, during the return at night, flying on instruments, air traffic control lost radio and radar contact," Pappalardo said, adding that there was no distress signal and "no attempt to eject".
[[nid:1561024]]
"With my husband, we felt the walls of our house shake a little before 11pm. We heard a kind of loud bang, like when an aircraft breaks the sound barrier, but worse," nearby resident Sandra Rotatinti told AFP.
Although they saw nothing, their neighbour, who was out walking his dog at the time, saw "a ball of fire in the sky" and called the fire brigade.
The plane crashed in a wooded area.
The two-seat Mirage 2000D fighter jet entered service in 1993. France has used it in conflicts in Kosovo in 1999, Libya in 2011, Afghanistan, Iraq, Syria and Africa's Sahel region.
Several have been involved in accidents. In January 2019, both crew members aboard one making a low-altitude night flight died in eastern France. In July 2021, the crew of another managed to eject when their aircraft went down near Nancy.
France has just completed a renovation programme for its fleet of Mirage 2000Ds, which it intends to keep in service into the 2030s.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nigeria Ebola case matches DR Congo strain
Article:
LAGOS: The Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain behind a major outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), officials said on Wednesday, marking the spread of the deadly disease to more parts of Africa.
The case, detected in a woman diplomat in Nigeria — the first there since the current outbreak in the DRC — has revived memories of a widespread outbreak in 2014 that struck several countries in the region.
Nigeria is the fourth African country affected by the outbreak, which this week spread across the continent, with Kenya in the east reporting nine cases since Oct 6.
The DRC's Ebola epidemic has become the deadliest in the country's history, killing 4,381 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases since mid-May, according to health authorities.
The patient in Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, travelled from Uganda to the capital, Abuja, on Oct 3, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said.
"We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo," said Olajumoke Babatunde, director of the public health laboratory service at the NCDC.
The World Health Organization (WHO) also confirmed that it was the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment.
"This person is actually a diplomat," another official said, adding that the patient's condition had deteriorated to "multi-organ failure". The official did not disclose the diplomat's nationality.
In August, Uganda was officially declared Ebola-free by the WHO after recording 20 cases — almost all of them in people who had travelled from the DRC.
Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) director-general Jean Kaseya warned on Tuesday of "an extremely serious threat", with fatality rates in the DRC rapidly approaching 50 per cent.
The Africa CDC has called a high-level meeting of health ministers for next Wednesday to assess the outbreak, coordinate cross-border efforts, support affected countries and strengthen continental preparedness.
[[nid:1561014]]
'Geographically widespread'
"This Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history, affecting multiple countries across three regions of Africa," Kaseya said, calling for urgent international action.
Nigeria has identified 44 contacts who are being monitored, while intensifying efforts to find others who may have been exposed.
The WHO said in a statement that infection prevention and control measures were being "ramped up" at the private hospital where the patient sought care.
Nigeria's successful containment of an Ebola outbreak in 2014 has raised confidence that the country can respond effectively to new public health threats.
That epidemic killed more than 11,000 people across West Africa between late 2013 and 2016.
In an interview with AFP, former NCDC director Abdulsalami Nasidi expressed confidence that Nigeria could contain the outbreak as it did 12 years ago, but said success would depend on funding and commitment from the presidency.
"Nigeria was able to rapidly control 2014 Ebola outbreak because they took the right actions at the right time, had good command structures on the ground," Nasidi said.
The response to the latest outbreak could test President Bola Tinubu's re-election bid as Nigeria prepares for presidential polls in January.
In a statement on Wednesday by Tinubu's media adviser, Bayo Onanuga, a presidential task force on Ebola said it was confident Nigeria would be "able to dent this outbreak".
2014 outbreak
In 2014, the first Nigerian case, detected in Lagos, the country's commercial hub of more than 20 million people, raised fears that the highly contagious virus would spread rapidly.
However, a swift response by Nigerian authorities, supported by international organisations, helped bring the epidemic under control within 21 days, resulting in only 19 infections and seven deaths.
"It was so shocking when we got the news yesterday," Anthony Ojogho, a 42-year-old civil servant, told AFP on the streets of Abuja on Wednesday morning.
But he was confident in the authorities' ability to contain the spread of the virus, citing Nigeria's previous experience.
Governments "have always been equal to the task. We contained Ebola, we contained coronavirus," he said.
"If the right steps are being taken, I'm very sure that we're going to contain to a large extent the spread of Ebola virus in Nigeria."
