Title: Protests banned in parts of Paris as Macron swipes at Trump
Article:
PARIS: Police banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday as France braced for more demonstrations, just days after student and other rallies degenerated into some of the worst street unrest in years.
The announcement on Wednesday came after President Emmanuel Macron took an apparent swipe at his US counterpart Donald Trump for exploiting the riots for political advantage in the US midterm election campaign.
The Paris ban will last from 8am to 8pm (0600 to 1800 GMT) and apply to key landmarks in the French capital, including the Elysee presidential palace, both houses of parliament, as well as tourist attractions such as the Louvre museum and the Champs-Elysees.
Other areas where rallies will be prohibited include Bastille and Republique squares, and the Chatelet-Les Halles shopping area, which was heavily targeted by looters over the weekend.
France has admitted it "lost control" amid the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings.
As his government struggled to contain a crisis that has damaged France's image abroad and rattled financial markets six months before presidential elections, Macron implied that Trump, and possibly Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is also fighting an election campaign, had made "stupid comments" on the unrest for political gain.
"There are people who campaign at France's expense — leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic," he told reporters in Doha.
Trump has sought to link the unrest to "migrants, jihadists, and communists" as he campaigned for his Republican Party in the US with an anti-immigration message.
He also praised French far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Tuesday. She shares his ideologies.
Le Pen late on Wednesday branded Macron's remarks as "conspiratorial" in a post on X.
"The images we saw last Saturday are not generated by artificial intelligence: they show the sad reality of what France has become after 10 years of Macronist rule," added the far-right candidate, who is leading in the polls for the 2027 presidential election.
Several analysts have dismissed claims that migrants were driving France's protests.
'New phase' upcoming
The unrest overshadowed demonstrations on Saturday, when more than half a million people marched nationwide against the cost of living. Those rallies followed four weeks of student protests that have closed many schools across France.
[[nid:1561033]]
Following the rioting — the worst France has seen in years — and ahead of fresh cost-of-living demonstrations planned for Saturday, Macron's government has warned it will brook no further violence.
Fresh demonstrations planned by high school pupils and university students were similarly banned in both Paris and the southeastern city of Lyon.
Following a meeting with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Wednesday, the leader of France's hardline CGT union, Sophie Binet, called for a "new phase" of protests, with strikes early next month.
Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said on Wednesday that, of the 2,500 people taken into custody during and after the protests, 174 had been jailed. Another 917 had been formally prosecuted, he added.
The upheaval in the EU's second-biggest economy has rattled financial markets already nervous about the country's growing debt pile and deficit.
The yield on France's benchmark 10-year bond passed 5 per cent on Wednesday as investors demanded a higher return amid fiscal concerns.
On Friday, ratings agency Moody's is expected to lower its rating on France's public debt.
'Quite disconcerting'
France's neighbours Italy and Belgium were also experiencing similar unrest, on a smaller scale. Italy's government has ordered 500 troops to Milan to stem street violence there.
While curfews imposed in several cities have helped calm the situation, they have disrupted some access to late-night public transport.
"It's quite disconcerting," said one Paris commuter who gave only his first name, Louis, when he found his line closed. But "if it can prevent further acts of vandalism... then yes, I think it's a good thing", he said.
The Yellow Vest movement behind last weekend's demonstrations announced on Wednesday that it planned a march on Saturday from Bastille square in Paris, followed by nationwide demonstrations on Nov 5.

Title: eBay to slash 1,000 more jobs, around 9 per cent of workforce
Article:
NEW YORK: US e-commerce platform eBay will cut about 1,000 jobs, or around 9 per cent of its workforce, a spokesperson told AFP on Wednesday, following an initial round of layoffs in February.
The company informed staff of the cuts on Tuesday, according to a statement from the spokesperson.
The step was taken "to ensure we continue to operate from a position of strength by aligning our teams and resources with our top strategic priorities", the spokesperson said, adding that eBay was "committed to supporting them through this transition with care and respect".
eBay had 12,300 employees at the end of 2025, before announcing a first round of layoffs in February affecting 800 jobs.
When presenting first- and second-quarter results earlier this year, executives at the San Jose, California-based company made no mention of the job cuts.
After several difficult years marked by near-stagnant revenue, eBay returned to growth in 2025 and saw an acceleration in the first half of this year.
In July, the group took control of clothing resale site Depop for US$1.2 billion, seeking to capitalise on the growth of the second-hand apparel market.
In early May, video game retailer GameStop made an unsolicited takeover offer valuing eBay at US$55.5 billion.
GameStop chief Ryan Cohen argued that the group was poorly managed and not innovative enough.
The board ultimately rejected the offer, with investors questioning how the deal would be financed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says fraud investigations make 'very big dent' in overseas scams
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday his administration had made a "very big dent" in scams by foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent investments, focusing on an anti-fraud message ahead of November's midterm elections.
Trump, members of his Cabinet and other senior administration officials met at the White House for an event on cybercrime prevention, where FBI Director Kash Patel said his agency had taken down 20 scam compounds worldwide.
Early voting has already begun in many states ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections, in which Trump's Republican Party risks losing control of Congress, while polls show that voters' top concern is the rising cost of living.
"Federal law enforcement has been able to warn over 10,000 Americans targeted for victimization, and we've prevented US$1.6 billion in losses — at least — this year," Trump said at the event.
Americans filed more than one million complaints with the FBI about internet scams last year, a 17 per cent increase from 2024, according to an FBI report.
Cabinet officials at the meeting included Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and Attorney General Todd Blanche, while White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller were also present.
The president's team highlighted efforts to crack down on overseas cryptocurrency scams, with Miller saying that Trump had "effectively declared cyber warfare against the cyber criminals".
Trump's family has been heavily involved in soliciting investments in cryptocurrency.
A Reuters investigation found that the Republican president and his sons had added at least US$2.3 billion to the family fortune through their main cryptocurrency ventures, while investors they had wooed had taken a US$2.3 billion hit.
White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly, in a statement to Reuters about the investigation, said: "All actions by President Trump and his administration are taken in the best interest of the American people."
Trump pardoned Changpeng Zhao, the convicted founder of cryptocurrency exchange Binance, in October 2025. Zhao had stepped down after the company pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering programme.
In a March executive order, Trump directed the Justice Department to prioritise identifying and prosecuting scammers who carry out crimes online. Trump later directed the Department of Homeland Security to work with private companies to surveil foreign criminal hacking groups.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump asks US Supreme Court to allow Big Bend border wall construction
Article:
NEW YORK: President Donald Trump's administration asked the US Supreme Court on Wednesday to let it proceed with a plan to build a US-Mexico border barrier in a remote region of West Texas that includes Big Bend National Park.
The Justice Department filed an emergency request asking the court to lift a federal judge's order halting wall construction in the region while a lawsuit against the project, brought by an environmental group and other challengers, proceeds.
The Republican president has long touted building or reinforcing barriers along the US-Mexico border as a signature part of his anti-immigration policies.
But his administration's push to extend border infrastructure into the national park, about 400km southeast of El Paso, has faced opposition from local officials, conservationists and some Texas Republicans.
The lawsuit was brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, a Big Bend-area river guide and a group seeking to preserve a historic church in Ruidosa, Texas, which says its fragile adobe structure is threatened by the border construction.
The plaintiffs challenged a series of waivers issued by the US Department of Homeland Security to expedite the construction of roads and barriers in the Big Bend region, bypassing various environmental and conservation laws.
Former Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem and current secretary Markwayne Mullin, who issued the waivers between February and July, found the region to be an "area of high illegal entry", requiring additional barriers to control the border.
US District Judge Kathleen Cardone in El Paso issued an injunction on Oct 2 halting construction. In an opinion issued later, the judge found that the waivers exceeded the authority of Noem and Mullin.
The Justice Department urged the Supreme Court to pause or overturn Cardone's injunction.
"Even assuming that the secretary's waiver authority implicates a question of 'vast economic and political significance,' Congress did clearly authorise the secretary both to build border barriers and to waive legal requirements in order to facilitate their expeditious construction," the Justice Department wrote.
In August, the administration paused construction in Big Bend after the project drew bipartisan criticism over its potential impact on the park's landscape and wildlife.
Crews had begun clearing land in the park for roads and border security infrastructure, prompting protests and lawsuits seeking to halt the work.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High cost may make families think twice
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) offers a competitive alternative to express buses and flights for time-conscious travellers, but families may find the combined ticket costs less attractive, transport experts said.
Universiti Malaya Centre for Transportation Research head Associate Professor Dr Yuen Choon Wah said the fares were attractive for students and solo travellers, with the journey from Gombak to Kota Baru expected to take about five hours compared with more than eight by bus.
"Even with train fares of RM125 compared with bus fares of RM50-plus, I still think it is worth the money," he said, adding that the service could encourage more travellers to switch to rail.
But he had doubts about whether the ECRL could attract group travellers, as the combined cost of tickets could make other options more economical.
One-way fares from Gombak to KotaSAS start at RM60 for the Transit service and RM68 for the Express service, while fares to Kota Baru start at RM125 (Transit) and RM147 (Express).
In comparison, express bus fares from Kuala Lumpur to Kota Baru range from RM34 to RM65, while premium services and peak-period tickets can cost up to RM105.
One-way flights between Kuala Lumpur and Kota Baru can range from RM89 to RM350 or more.
Universiti Teknologi Mara Faculty of Film, Theatre and Animation's Associate Professor Dr Mohd Syuhaidi Abu Bakar said the fares were reasonable and competitive when journey time, comfort and convenience were considered.
"Some people may consider the fares expensive, but we have to consider the time saved, the comfort and convenience."
He said road journeys to Kelantan could take long hours, particularly along the Kuala Lipis-Merapoh-Gua Musang trunk road.
During festive seasons, such journeys can take over 16 hours.
He said the ECRL could provide a good alternative, although affordability would remain an important consideration.
Malaysia Institute of Transport director Associate Professor Dr Mohd Fathi Abu Yaziz @ Mohamad said the ECRL should not be assessed solely on fares, but also on reliability, comfort and time savings.
"The service can bridge the gap between air travel and road transport by providing a faster alternative to buses without the airport procedures."
He cautioned that dynamic pricing could affect affordability for lower-income passengers.
He suggested a hybrid pricing model, with measures such as regulated fare caps or concessions, to balance revenue considerations with the need to keep rail travel accessible.

Title: New genus of tiny crustacean discovered in Sipadan cave
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SEMPORNA: A tiny crustacean found in a submerged cave off Pulau Sipadan has turned out to be from a new species and an entirely new genus.
Named Sipadanomolgus dissimilis, the copepod was collected using a light trap inside the marine cave called Turtle Tomb at the world-renowned diving destination.
Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's Associate Professor Dr Azman Abdul Rahim, who led the research, said: "The researchers established an entirely new genus, Sipadanomolgus, as the specimen exhibits a distinct combination of anatomical features that does not fit the existing genera within the family."
The research was conducted under the Ocean Census programme, a global initiative to document marine life, in collaboration with Dr Chaichat Boonyanusith of Nakhon Ratchasima Rajabhat University and Dr Koraon Wongkamhaeng of Kasetsart University, both in Thailand.
The findings were published in the European Journal of Taxonomy on Tuesday.
The discovery builds on previous finds in Turtle Tomb, underscoring the scientific value of exploring specialised marine habitats.
Azman said it also broadened understanding of Sipadan's biodiversity beyond its famous coral reefs and larger marine animals, highlighting the role of less visible, cave-dwelling organisms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Women hold 34pc of top board seats
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Women account for more than 34.4 per cent of board seats among Malaysia's top 100 publicly listed companies, but the next challenge is ensuring their representation translates into greater influence over corporate strategy and decision-making.
The 30% Club Malaysia said corporate leaders must move beyond meeting diversity targets to building boardrooms where women's perspectives help shape business priorities, strengthen governance and drive sustainable growth.
Its chair and PwC Malaysia executive chair, Nurul A'in Abdul Latif, said aspiring women directors needed greater access to professional networks, sponsorship and boardroom exposure to prepare them for leadership roles.
"Through mentorship and meaningful connections, the Board Mentoring Scheme (BMS) helps develop a sustainable pipeline of board-ready women who can contribute effectively in governance and leadership roles."
She said achieving gender-balanced leadership required male allies to sponsor talent and create more inclusive pathways to leadership.
She was speaking at the organisation's annual Board Mentoring Celebration on Tuesday, themed "Beyond the Numbers: From Representation to Real Influence".
The event marked the completion of the programme's 11th cohort, comprising 15 women, and welcomed 24 participants to its 12th cohort.
Established with PwC Malaysia in 2017, the nine-month BMS pairs aspiring women leaders with experienced board directors to boost their governance knowledge and professional networks.
The scheme has supported more than 179 senior women leaders across 11 cohorts, with 47 per cent securing board positions in public-listed companies, small and medium enterprises, and industry associations.
30% Club Malaysia steering committee member and PwC Malaysia partner Pauline Ho said board diversity should be measured by whether women's views influenced organisational decisions, rather than representation alone.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India urged to cease 'use of excessive force' to curb protests
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
WASHINGTON: United Nations experts called on Tuesday for an independent investigation into Indian authorities' conduct in a recent crackdown on protests, where they said demonstrators sustained injuries and some reported being subjected to ill-treatment.
Opposition parties and student organisations held protests in recent weeks, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter ​lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Mass protests also took place in the summer over exam-paper leaks and led to the resignation of the education minister.
"Despite the non-violent nature of the assemblies, law enforcement agencies have reportedly deployed force against unarmed students, including lathi charges, and have prevented thousands from joining the protests," the two dozen independent experts said, referring to batons used to break up crowds.
"We call on the authorities to immediately cease the use of excessive force, rescind blanket assembly bans and refrain from the misuse of digital surveillance, including through biometrics, and Internet disruptions."
India has dismissed such criticism and cast it as interference in its internal affairs, including when the UN human rights office this month expressed concerns over mass detentions over the latest protests.
The government said this month that law enforcement acted "strictly in accordance with the law".
Protesting groups said the removal of 130 million names from voter lists led to eligible voters being disenfranchised, which disproportionately affected poor and homeless people, as well as ethnic minorities, including Muslims, who are unlikely to vote for the Hindu nationalist BJP.
The BJP ​and the Election Commission deny this.
The commission said it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error could pursue appeals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Axe attack on teacher in Kuching: Student released on police bail
Article:
KUCHING: A Form Four student arrested over an attack on a female teacher at an international school in Kuching has been released on police bail.
The teacher
was injured
in the incident 8am today.
Sarawak Acting Sarawak police commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said police were investigating the incident.
"Police are investigating and collecting evidence. Additional details will be issued by the Kuching district police chief," he said in a statement today, adding that the student had been released on police bail.
The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code and Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957.
A video showing the student attacking the teacher went viral earlier.
In a statement, Tunku Putra HELP said it had reviewed its safety protocols and strengthened security measures following the incident.
The international school will reopen on Thursday with three ancillary police officers stationed on campus.

Title: Intern found dead in Port Dickson died from fall from height, police say no foul play
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Oct 22 — A final-year college student undergoing practical training at a hotel in Lukut was found dead behind an eatery here yesterday.
Port Dickson District Police Chief Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan said the 21-year-old man was found at 6.05 am after police received an emergency call via the MERS 999 line from a member of the public.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim had facial injuries and a broken arm, believed to have been sustained in a fall from a building.
“The post-mortem found that the cause of death was head and abdominal injuries resulting from a fall from a height.
“Investigations also found no criminal elements in the case,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Ahmad Afiq said the victim was believed to have been staying in a rented room in a three-storey building used as a hostel near where the body was found.
An inspection of the room found no signs of a break-in, and no valuables or personal documents were missing.
The victim’s body was taken to Port Dickson Hospital, and the case has been classified as sudden death (SDR).
Members of the public with information about the incident are urged to assist with the investigation.
They are also advised against speculation out of respect for the victim’s family. — Bernama

Title: Hold off on trips to France for now, MOHE tells Malaysian students in Europe amid riots
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — All 462 Malaysian students currently pursuing their studies in France are reported to be safe, with none involved or directly affected by the demonstrations and riots occurring in several major cities across the country, including Paris.
The Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE) said that the academic activities of Malaysian students in that country are continuing as usual, while educational institutions in the affected areas have shifted to online learning.
According to the MOHE, its team – through the Education Attaché Office in Paris, in collaboration with the Foreign Ministry, the Embassy of Malaysia in Paris, and sponsoring agencies – is continuously monitoring the situation to ensure the safety and well-being of the Malaysian students.
“To date, there are 462 Malaysian students pursuing their studies in France, and no reports have been received regarding any students being involved or directly affected by the demonstrations and riots taking place in several major cities, including Paris,” the MOHE said in a statement.
In light of these developments, the MOHE has advised Malaysian students in France to avoid affected areas, comply with the instructions of local authorities and stay updated through official announcements.
At the same time, the MOHE has advised Malaysian students currently in other European countries to postpone any travel to France until the situation is brought back under control.
The ministry has emphasised that continuous monitoring will be carried out in collaboration with relevant parties to ensure the safety and well-being of all Malaysian students in France are upheld.
The MOHE also urges parents and families of the students to remain calm and obtain information from official sources, while ensuring that their children adhere to the safety guidelines issued by the Education Attaché Office in Paris and the Embassy of Malaysia in Paris.
Any inquiries or requests for further information may be directed via email to maisarah.isa@jpa.gov.my or eml@mohe.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Classes resume: Kuching international school beefs up security with three police officers after teacher attacked
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 22 — Tunku Putra-HELP (TPH) International School has confirmed that it will immediately enhance its campus security measures, including stationing three ancillary police officers on its grounds, following an incident where a teacher was injured by a student yesterday.
The school management announced that safety checks will be conducted upon entry to the campus with immediate effect, as part of a broader review to implement long-term security measures in consultation with relevant authorities.
“While existing safety measures remain in place, TPH has reviewed its safety protocols and has enhanced security measures in consultation with the relevant authorities.
“The school is also exploring more comprehensive, long-term security measures for the campus.
“The Senior Leadership Team will hold assemblies for students to address the incident, provide assurance, respond appropriately to their concerns and provide counselling support for those who may need it,” the school posted on its official Facebook account yesterday.
TPH also confirmed that the school will resume classes tomorrow after receiving clearance from all relevant authorities, following an early closure today as a precautionary measure advised by the police.
Providing an update on the victim, the school stated that the injured teacher was taken to the hospital by ambulance and is currently recovering well with no critical injuries.
It clarified that the alleged student is in police custody and is no longer an active student of TPH, while urging the public not to circulate unverified information or speculate on the incident.
Earlier, Acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak confirmed the male Form Four student’s arrest and revealed that police seized a penknife and a small axe in connection with the case.
He added that the student has been released on police bail and the case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for causing hurt with dangerous weapons, as well as Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: DCP stands for Deputy Commissioner of Police.

Title: From pocket money to cooking: How MOE hopes to make maths less scary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) plans to strengthen the competencies of mathematics teachers through targeted training and the strategic placement of qualified mathematics teachers.
This initiative aims to enhance students’ mastery of the subject and their ability to apply mathematics in daily life.
Deputy director of the Science and Mathematics Sector at MOE’s Curriculum Development Division Dr Aszunarni Ayob said that the Mathematics Teacher Competency Standards – developed under the Malaysia Mathematics Education Transformation Plan (RTPMM) 2026-2035 – will allow for training programmes to be tailored to the specific needs and competency levels of individual teachers.
“Through these standards, we will be able to gauge the competency levels of our teachers, which will then allow us to provide them with targeted training.
“We will not implement a ‘one-size-fits-all’ training programme for all teachers,” she said while as a guest on the Bernama TV programme Ruang Bicara entitled “RTPMM 2026-2035: Nurturing a Mathematically Literate Generation,” here last evening.
She said teachers with expertise in the field will be appointed as ‘Mathematics Specialists’ to mentor their peers.
Furthermore, several Teacher Education Institutes (IPG) will be designated as centres for mathematics education, focusing on teacher training in this specific domain.
Aszunarni said the deployment of teachers specialising in mathematics is being coordinated to ensure their expertise is utilised optimally.
This aligns with the six core pillars of the RTPMM, which encompass governance, curriculum and assessment, teacher competency, co-curricular activities and support, infrastructure, and collaborative networks.
She explained that the understanding of mathematical concepts will be strengthened under the 2027 School Curriculum (KP2027) through a Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract approach.
Meanwhile, the ‘Bilik Darjah Fikrah’ approach encourages students to articulate their problem-solving processes and provide justifications for their answers.
She further mentioned that in secondary schools, emphasis is placed on both calculator-assisted and non-calculator calculations.
This is intended to strike a balance between mental arithmetic skills – such as mental calculation and estimation – and the ability to solve more complex problems.
“As part of the RTPMM, we intend to develop an integrated virtual hub for teaching resources.
“This is designed to facilitate easier access to these materials for both teachers and students.
“This is because we actually possess a wealth of materials, and we aim to integrate these resources into a single platform that is easily accessible to both students and teachers,” she said.
Aszunarni stated that the mathematics education network will also be strengthened through the involvement of universities, agencies, the industry and community, who will share their expertise and demonstrate the application of mathematics across various fields.
She noted that efforts to foster students’ interest and confidence also require the support of school administrators, counsellors, teachers of other subjects and parents.
This includes incorporating mathematical elements into co-curricular activities and daily life — such as managing pocket money or measuring ingredients for cooking.
“In reality, one way to spark their interest in mathematics is to help them understand that mathematics is all around them.
“That is the most important thing.
“We want them to grasp that mathematics is everywhere.
“Only then will they be able to appreciate it, rather than feel afraid of it,” she said.
She added that the RTPMM will be implemented in phases: beginning with the strengthening of foundations and readiness; followed by enhancement and expansion; and finally moving towards consolidation and impact assessment — all with the goal of producing a mathematically literate generation. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: RTPMM stands for Rancangan Transformasi Pendidikan Matematik Malaysia, or the Malaysia Mathematics Education Transformation Plan.
IPG stands for Institut Pendidikan Guru, or the Teacher Education Institutes.
KP2027 stands for Kurikulum Persekolahan 2027, or the 2027 School Curriculum.

Title: Melaka seat deal done: BN takes 21, PAS and allies get seven
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 22 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will contest 21 seats while PAS and its allies will contest seven in next month’s Melaka state election, following the finalisation of negotiations between the parties.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition would use its own logo in the election, while the decision on the logo to be used by PAS and its allies would be left to their leadership.
“BN will contest using the BN logo. It is up to their (PAS and its allies’) leadership to decide,” he told reporters after attending the ‘Melaka Bermunajat: Ratib Al-Attas and Asmaulhusna’ programme at Masjid Salmah Khamis in Masjid Tanah here last night.
Ahmad Zahid said BN would announce its candidates for the Melaka polls this Saturday.
The Election Commission (EC) has set polling day for the Melaka state election on Nov 14, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats contested, enabling the coalition to form the state government. Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured two. — Bernama

Title: In the Dewan Rakyat today: API accuracy, missing Malaysians in Nepal and GovTech
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The achievements of GovTech Malaysia, the status of Malaysians who remain unreachable following flash floods in Nepal, and the accuracy of Malaysia’s official Air Pollutant Index (API) readings are among the key issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today.
According to the Order Paper on the Parliament’s official portal, during the Ministers’ Question Time (MQT), Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong) will ask the Digital Minister to outline GovTech Malaysia’s achievements in advancing the country’s digital transformation agenda.
She will also seek details on the success of strategic collaborations with other ministries in improving service delivery to the public and business sector, as well as the agency’s plans to strengthen the digital government ecosystem.
Meanwhile, Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) will ask the Foreign Minister for an update on Malaysians who remain unreachable following flash floods that struck Nepal’s Rasuwa district on Aug 26.
Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara) will ask the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister to explain the measures taken to ensure that official API readings remain accurate, transparent and trusted by the public.
He will also seek clarification on whether the government plans to improve the dissemination of air quality information to make it easier for the public to understand and more responsive to changing haze conditions.
Meanwhile, during the oral question session, Datuk Siti Aminah Aching (BN-Beaufort) will ask the Minister of Finance the number of pickup truck and jeep owners in Sabah who have received the additional 100-litre allocation under the BUDI Diesel initiative.
She will also seek details on assistance for owners who use the vehicles for small businesses, agricultural activities or travel to rural areas.
Datuk Seri Sh Mohmed Puzi Sh Ali (BN-Pekan) will ask the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister for details of the enforcement outcomes under Ops Tiris Bersepadu, particularly in border areas, including the number of cases, value of leakages, seizures and arrests.
He will also seek an explanation on weaknesses in enforcement that have allowed repeated smuggling incidents, as well as measures to close loopholes, strengthen border controls and dismantle smuggling syndicates.
Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) will ask the Women, Family and Community Development Minister to state the number of women aged between 25 and 59 who are outside the labour force due to caregiving responsibilities, including caring for children, older persons and other family members.
She will also seek clarification on the economic value of unpaid care work to the country and when a national care economy ecosystem will be established.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting will subsequently continue with the policy-level debate on the Supply Bill 2027, following its tabling by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, on Oct 9.
According to the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-level debate on the 2027 Budget is scheduled from Oct 12 to 22, followed by a four-day winding-up session by the relevant ministers beginning on Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sitting is scheduled to run for 37 days, until Dec 8. — Bernama

Title: Three in 10 couples set on divorce changed their minds after counselling, says Family’s Ministry sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Thirty per cent of couples who intended to divorce reconciled after undergoing family counselling sessions managed by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN).
Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) secretary-general Datuk Dr Maziah Che Yusoff said the achievement demonstrated that counselling could help couples better understand domestic conflicts and reconsider their decision to separate.
“Although the rate may seem small, it is a significant achievement for us, considering that the initiative only began last year,” she said while appearing as a guest on the Kasih Lensa Keluarga podcast produced by Bernama TV at Wisma Bernama yesterday.
She said poor communication between husbands and wives was among the main causes of domestic conflict.
Counselling sessions provide a space for couples to manage their emotions, communicate openly and reassess the impact of their conflicts on their marriage and their children’s future.
“Sometimes, the root cause of a dispute is not particularly significant, yet it affects the emotions of both parties. When a couple sits down to discuss matters calmly, they can see the bigger picture regarding the future of their family and marriage,” she said.
Maziah said KPWKM would continue to improve family intervention services based on findings and experiences from existing programmes.
She said efforts to strengthen the family institution were central to the National Family Compassion Policy (DKKN) 2026-2030, launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Feb 14.
The policy translates the National Social Policy into efforts to address increasingly complex family challenges and social issues.
“DKKN is based on five core Kasih values, namely Affection (Kasih Sayang), Trust (Amanah), Health (Sihat), Knowledge (Ilmu) and Harmony (Harmoni). It also encompasses five strategic thrusts involving the marriage institution, family planning, parenting quality, inclusive family support and conflict management,” she said.
Commenting on modern parenting challenges, Maziah said children were influenced not only by their home environment but also by digital technology, social media, schools and peers.
“In the past, a well-behaved child would simply stay at home. Today, however, a child alone in their room is not necessarily safe from outside influences because of smartphones,” she said.
She said strengthening the family institution required cooperation among the government, communities and schools, rather than placing the entire responsibility on parents.
Meanwhile, she invited the public to attend the National Family Day celebration in Shah Alam on Nov 6 and 7, which will feature various family-related programmes and exhibitions. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: LPPKN stands for Lembaga Penduduk dan Pembangunan Keluarga Negara, or the National Population and Family Development Board.
KPWKM stands for Kementerian Pembangunan Wanita, Keluarga dan Masyarakat, or the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development.
DKKN stands for Dasar Kasih Keluarga Negara, or the National Family Compassion Policy.

Title: How Malaysians can have enough money after retiring: Moving away from choosing EPF ‘lump sum’ payouts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — If you are given a pot of money, would you spend it all in one go or over just a few years, or would you make it last for the rest of your life?
Shifting away from lump-sum EPF withdrawals towards lifelong income
At the recent Employees Provident Fund (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 (ISWC 2026), global pension expert William Price said the idea of accessing retirement savings as a lump sum is deeply embedded in Malaysian society, partly because of expectations or plans to help one's children pay for their education, a house or a wedding, for example.
Price said, however, that viewing retirement savings as a “pot of assets” could almost blind people into thinking they have a lot of money, while focusing on it as “income” would provide a “reality check”.
While people tend to have more savings and a greater ability to work or remain active in the early years of retirement, he noted that OECD data showed older people (aged 76 and above) were poorer on average in virtually all OECD countries.
In an interview with
Malay Mail
, Price proposed three possible solutions for Malaysia:
1. Introduce a non-contributory pension, raise the retirement age and increase the EPF withdrawal age
(If there is an integrated reform of both private and public pensions)
Unlike a defined-contribution retirement savings scheme such as the EPF, where members contribute to their own retirement savings, a non-contributory pension provides retirement benefits without requiring recipients to have made contributions.
Price said non-contributory pensions had been fundamental to reducing old-age poverty in other countries, noting that some people were unpaid carers or unable to work.
“And you just have to accept there will be some people, in the way that some people never work; some people are disabled; some people are lifetime poor; some people were working non-stop, but just not paid because they were caring or whatever the circumstances were,” he said at ISWC 2026.
William Price, a former global pension expert with the World Bank who has also worked with the UK Treasury and UK Pensions Regulator, said Malaysia could raise its retirement age and EPF withdrawal age while introducing a tax-funded pension from age 75. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Price proposed that the government introduce a tax-funded “non-contributory pension” for all Malaysians aged 75 and above, providing a minimum income sufficient to cover basic living expenses, such as groceries.
“So if there was an integrated reform, what I would do is that there would be a non-contributory pension for everyone at 75,” he told
Malay Mail
, adding that it could be taxable for wealthy recipients or tax-free for those relying on it as their sole source of income.
Why 75? Price said introducing non-contributory pensions from that age would be more affordable, as the population aged 75 and above is relatively smaller than those aged 60 or 65 and above.
Currently, Malaysia's minimum retirement age is 60, while Malaysians can choose to withdraw their entire EPF savings or make monthly or partial withdrawals from as early as age 55.
Alongside the proposed government-funded pension kicking in at 75, he also suggested raising both the retirement age and the age at which members can access their EPF savings as a lump sum to 60 or 65.
This would help people preserve their savings for longer and ensure they have sufficient income until at least age 75.
“So you say to people, ‘your money has to last until 75 at least’. And so they’ve got a kind of a fixed window of time. They’re like ‘okay, so I need to save enough to mean that I’ve got enough until I’m aged 75, and then the government will give me ‘X’,” the CEO of pension consultancy firm D3P Global told
Malay Mail
.
Those who feel the proposed non-contributory pension would be insufficient to meet their needs after age 75 could plan to retain some of their EPF savings beyond that age, allowing them to rely on a combination of both income sources in later life.
2. Set aside some EPF savings to generate income from age 75 onwards
(If there is no integrated reform of the public and private pension systems)
In a scenario where the government does not introduce a non-contributory pension, Price proposed that Malaysians set aside part of their EPF savings to provide an income after turning 75.
In his ISWC presentation, Price illustrated how a retiree could make withdrawals from their pension savings over a 10-year period (say, from age 65 to 75), while a portion of their retirement balance is used each year to fund a “deferred annuity” that would provide income for the rest of their life after turning 75.
Noting that the actual method would depend on what people find acceptable, Price outlined to
Malay Mail
several possible options:
Set a minimum level of EPF savings that everyone must have by age 75, with part of their EPF savings transferred to a fund for those aged 75 and above (75+ fund) from age 60 or 65 onwards.
Savings not transferred to the 75+ fund could still be accessed before age 75.
Savings transferred to the fund could only be accessed after age 75, but would go to beneficiaries if the member dies before reaching that age.
Begin transferring savings to the 75+ fund at an earlier age, such as 35, 40 or 45.
Transfer only the annual EPF dividends, for example, from age 55 or 60 onwards, to the 75+ fund.
Price explained that there was nothing “magic” about the number 75 and that the proposal could also be used to ensure an income from other ages, such as 70.
“So, the number kind of depends on the population and the amount of savings they have. But because lots of people don't have a lot of EPF savings, you can't really afford to have a guaranteed minimum from age 60 until you die. It's just too expensive,” he told
Malay Mail.
As for the EPF withdrawal age, he said it could be raised gradually, first from 55 to 60 and eventually to 65.
A variable annuity could help ensure retirees continue receiving an income throughout their lives. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
3. Introduce a variable annuity designed to provide income for life
Price said the EPF currently pools or shares investment risk among its members, but does not pool longevity risk.
In other words, members face the risk of living longer than their EPF savings can last.
He proposed that the EPF introduce a variable annuity, under which members would share both investment and longevity risks.
Under this proposal, members would have access to only a portion of their EPF savings, such as 10 per cent or 25 per cent, while the EPF would invest the remainder to generate lifelong income.
“The majority of your EPF money is invested. And from the age of 60 or 65, you are paid an income which will last until you die, and the amount of that income will depend on the balances that you have, the amount of savings you have,” he said, adding that the EPF could continue managing the investments as it currently does.
Explaining the pooling of mortality or longevity risk, Price said no one could predict how long they would live.
“So the people who die young get less; the people who die much later, they still get the income until they die. So you don't have to deal with the risk that you may live too long and outlive your savings,” he told
Malay Mail
.
He said income from the variable annuity could be taxable or tax-free, depending on the recipient's wealth.
Typically, with insured fixed annuities, insurance companies assume the longevity risk and guarantee a fixed annual payment until a person's death in exchange for a lump-sum payment.
Under Price's proposal, however, the annual income paid through a variable annuity would not be fixed but would depend on both investment performance and how long people in the pool live.
“If everyone is living longer than we expected, your annual payments will be a bit lower,” he said, adding that the lifelong payouts could be recalculated annually or based on an average.
Price said Malaysia could adopt any of the “three basic ideas” he had proposed as solutions.
“And it just depends which is the most politically acceptable and achievable.”

Title: Instead of a lump sum EPF withdrawal, how an automatic annuity with opt-out option could work for Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Licensed financial planner Rajen Devadason said an insurance annuity scheme like Singapore’s CPF LIFE could also work in Malaysia.
He explained that if the government gives a long runway, and make it politically more palatable by using automatic enrolment and giving people a chance to opt out, a similar scheme may be acceptable.
He was speaking to
Malay Mail
at the sidelines of the recent Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 (ISWC 2026).
Rajen said there might be the risk of a political backlash if access or withdrawals from EPF savings at ages 50, 55 and 60 is changed so one possibility is to keep the same withdrawal rules while using a small portion of EPF savings for an annuity.
“But if let’s say you increase your retirement age to 65 and you don’t change the withdrawal parameters at 50, 55, and 60, people are cool, no problems.
“But if you then give people the opportunity to work longer, that funding between 60 and 65, if all of that flowed into an annuity, that might work, might help,” he added.
Rajen believes something like an annuity insurance would be a “step in the right direction” for Malaysia, based on global experience.
“But by itself, it’s not enough. People must take personal responsibility. They have to build their own private pensions,” he said, adding that this should run in parallel with working longer.
“The whole purpose of working longer is that you can build a higher pile of retirement savings,” he said, also saying these funds should be used as capital to create multiple streams of passive income for retirement.
ILO senior social protection specialist Mariko Ouchi said different countries have different problems which means they would need their own pension solutions. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
No ‘one size fits all’ when designing retirement or pension systems
International Labour Organisation’s (ILO) senior social protection specialist for South Asia Mariko Ouchi said there is no “one perfect model” or “one fit for all” pension model in the world.
“Many people ask me what is the best model or good practice in terms of pension and old-age benefit in the world. And then I answer, all countries are having problems in one way or another. So, there is no ‘one perfect model’ as such,” she said in her presentation at the ISWC 2026.
She said each country will have to find solutions best suited to their different circumstances: “Malaysia has to seek its own solution to provide the best income guarantee for the elderly people.”
Ouchi said countries go through many changes, such as the different work nature including international jobs done remotely; migration; demography; higher life expectancies; higher retirement ages; and higher pension access ages.
She added it is important for countries to carry out periodic reviews or periodic actuarial evaluation on a country’s old-age benefit model (such as every three years or every five years) depending on the country and its system’s stability.
Countries also need to carry out a mid-term to long-term revisiting of their existing pension models, to see if it could continue running for decades unchanged or if substantial reforms are needed, Ouchi explained.

Title: As Singaporeans live longer, a look at how they manage their retirement savings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Singapore’s Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) deputy CEO (services) Wong Yan Jun said Singapore’s CPF — the equivalent of Malaysia’s EPF — had in 1987 introduced a phased withdrawal scheme.
The Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS) splits up monthly payouts of a Singaporean’s retirement savings over a fixed duration of 20 years to make it last longer.
This was because the government realised the lump sum withdrawal option at age 55 was less suited to support retirement over many years, as Singaporeans were living longer.
Singapore in 2007 recognised that more than half of Singaporean men and women would live past 82 and 85 respectively, which led to the 2009 introduction of the national longevity insurance annuity scheme, “CPF Lifelong Income for the Elderly” (CPF LIFE).
Back in 2007, many Singaporeans wrote to CPFB to challenge the idea that half of Singaporeans would live past 85, pointing out that most obituaries then showed people dying at ages like 75 and 80.
“But the truth is what we are preparing for is not for that moment. CPF LIFE is preparing for the future generation to come,” he said, adding that Singapore ultimately managed to push it through.
He said CPF LIFE pools the longevity risk to give Singaporeans the confidence that they can have income for as long as they live.
When asked at the Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 (ISWC 2026) panel session if CPF LIFE would need government subsidies to sustain lifetime payouts, he said the scheme is fully self-sustainable as the entire CPF LIFE funds are invested in Special Singapore Government Securities (SSGS) with a guaranteed risk-free return of about four per cent.
He also said CPF LIFE has very low expenses as compared to annuities provided by the private sector, as CPFB is a non-profit organisation and does not have intermediary fees such as agents’ commissions.
He said CPF LIFE’s monthly payouts are not a guaranteed or fixed number, which provides flexibility to adjust monthly payouts if necessary to ensure that the scheme can continue to be self-sustaining.
According to CPFB’s website, CPF members can join CPF LIFE anytime from age 65 and up to one month before turning 80.
CPF LIFE automatically includes those born after 1958 and with a minimum S$60,000 in CPF retirement savings by age 65, with Wong telling
Malay Mail
that nine in 10 CPF members are expected to reach this savings level by 2035.
Wong said those who do not meet the minimum S$60,000 level would be on the RSS plan (where payouts are only while savings last), but noted they can still opt in for CPF Life.
Those automatically included under CPF Life cannot be exempted from it, unless they have a pension or commercial annuity that gives the same or higher monthly payouts.
